newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran welcomes ceasefire between Iraqi Kurds.
newsitem.headline: Iran welcomes ceasefire between Iraqi Kurds.

text.p: Iran has told Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) leader Jalal Talabani it welcomed the U.S.-brokered ceasefire between the PUK and a rival Iraqi Kurdish group.

The official Iranian news agency IRNA reported on Monday that Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati, at a meeting with Talabani in Tehran on Sunday, "expressed content that the leaders of the two (Kurdish) groups had agreed on a ceasefire".

It said Talabani praised Iran for extending humanitarian assistance to tens of thousands of Kurdish refugees who fled to Iran to escape the fighting, which was halted by a U.S.-brokered ceasefire last week.
Delegations from the PUK and the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) are to meet in Turkey this week for peace talks chaired by senior U.S. diplomat Robert Pelletreau.
Diplomats say The KDP's military alliance with Baghdad and its charges that Talabani receives military backing from Iran will be issues of contention at the negotiations.
Iran has repeatedly denied it was helping Talabani and has called for an end to fighting.
